discovery: Optical detection and coherent control of single solid-state spins (nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond) and their use in quantum sensing
subfield: Quantum physics / condensed matter (solid-state spin qubits and quantum sensing)
motivation: Wrachtrup and colleagues first optically detected magnetic resonance of a single defect spin in diamond, and with Jelezko demonstrated coherent control, Rabi oscillations, nuclear-spin registers and single-shot readout of individual electron and nuclear spins at room temperature. This turned an isolated atomic-scale defect into a controllable qubit in a solid. Lukin, with these groups, proposed and realised nanoscale magnetometry with single NV spins, coupled electron spins to nuclear quantum memories, and established spin-photon entanglement for quantum networks. Their work opened a new field: solid-state quantum sensing that now images magnetic fields in condensed-matter systems, single molecules and living cells with nanometre resolution. It also launched the broader search for defect qubits in silicon carbide and other hosts, as well as loophole-free Bell tests and quantum-network nodes. It is a rare case of fundamental quantum control becoming a widely used measurement technology.
